summary:
M3 template builder (BRD A3) is built on the RLS-scoped client only, with no DB, shared-file or dependency changes. Both pages call requireScaleUp(['super_admin','fund_admin']) and use canManageTemplates.

/admin/templates lists each template (default first), with a strip showing the current version (published date and who published it), the months it is used for and the draft status with its count of unpublished changes. It has 'Create draft from current' (create_template_draft, then opens the editor) or 'Continue draft'. 'Make default' only appears when there is more than one template. The versions table shows version, TEMPLATE_STATUS_META badge, published at/by (name, or 'System' for the seed), months used (compressed ranges such as 'Jul–Sep 2026' from reporting_periods), section and field counts, notes, and a View/Edit link.

/admin/templates/[versionId]:
- Header: status badge and who started or published the version. Drafts get 'Discard draft' (ConfirmDialog) and 'Publish'. A published version gets 'Create draft from this version' (or 'Continue draft' if one exists); an archived one gets 'View current version'. Non-drafts show a read-only notice.
- Status panel: for a draft, whether it can be published (blocking issues and warnings) and the list of changes against the published version; for published or archived versions, the changes against the previous version plus the release notes.
- Structure editor, on wide screens next to a sticky live preview (a Structure/Preview switch below that width).
- Sections: move up/down, add (narrative / additional numbers / founder pulse, with a Position select that defaults to a sensible place), rename and describe (system sections too), and delete non-system sections with confirmation. System sections have a lock with tooltip 'System section - always part of the form'.
- Fields: move up/down, add and edit in a dialog, delete with confirmation. The dialog has label; a key auto-generated from the label, editable, unique in the version and never a built-in key; type limited to the section kind (narrative → long_text/text/picklist/tags/boolean/rating, custom_numbers → currency/number/integer/percent, pulse → rating/long_text/tags/picklist); required; help text; options one per line for picklist/tags; rating lowest/highest (whole numbers 0–10) with a label per value; limits (allow negative, min, max) or a maximum text length.
- System fields show a lock with tooltip 'System field - used in calculations' and keep their key, type, 'required' flag and section.
- 'New' badges mark sections and fields added since the base version.
- Publish needs release notes. Its ConfirmDialog explains that months opened from now on use this version while months already opened (latest named) keep theirs, and that the previous version will be archived.
- The preview is a static, non-focusable mock of the monthly form (required markers, help text, mock controls per type, options and scale labels, KPI and revenue-line notes). It refreshes after every saved change.
- Loading skeletons, a templates error boundary (retry) and a version not-found page are included.

Twelve Server Actions live in actions.ts: create/discard/publish draft, set default, add/update/delete/move section, add/update/delete/move field. Each follows assertScaleUp → zod v4 → rules → RLS write → revalidatePath → ok, with catch → toActionError. Actions load rows by id so a version id from the browser is never trusted. They check the version is still a draft with a friendly message, and treat a write that returns no row as stale ('the draft may have been published or discarded… reload'). Unique-key races become a field error. Database rule messages (P0001/42501) are shown as they are. The pure rules (keys, types per kind, options/limits JSON, readiness, change list, sort-order planning, month ranges) are in _lib/rules.ts and are shared by the dialogs and the actions.
deviations: System fields: besides label, help text and order, their number limits can also be edited (min/max, and 'allow negative' for gross and net profit only). This follows BRD B26 and ARCHITECTURE §2.2 (updated: 'Their validation may be changed'); the brief says label, help and order only. Key, type, 'required' flag and section stay locked. Revenue, cash, burn and the headcounts always stay non-negative (shown as a built-in rule).

Release notes are required to publish (ConfirmDialog requireReason). publish_template_version has no notes argument, so the action updates template_versions.notes (the only column authenticated users may update) and then calls the RPC. The two calls are not atomic: if publishing then fails, the notes stay on the draft, which is harmless.

Extra builder rule for data continuity: a field whose key an earlier published or archived version used keeps that key and type in the draft, because answers are stored per key across months. A new field may reuse an old key only with the same type. Keys of fields new in the draft stay editable.

Interpretations of the brief: no fields can be added to the system sections (Financials, Headcount, Company KPIs); a section's kind is fixed after creation; fields cannot move between sections (delete and re-add instead).

Additions not in the brief: 'Discard draft' (the database allows deleting drafts); 'Make default' (shown only when more than one template exists, as a single templates update per §2.2); a Position select when adding a section; the list of changes against the previous version and 'New' badges; client and server readiness checks that also block picklists/tags without options, rating scales whose highest value isn't above the lowest, and min > max, on top of the database's system section and field rule.

Builder limits: rating scale whole numbers 0–10 with labels of up to 60 characters; at most 100 options of 200 characters, no case-insensitive duplicates; maximum text length 1–20,000; label 200, help 1,000, section title 120, description 1,000, notes 2,000 characters.

New custom number fields start with negatives refused (stored as allow_negative: false); the admin can switch this on. A stored field with no limits set still reads as 'negatives allowed', which is how the database treats it.
Page props are typed explicitly as { params: Promise<{ versionId: string }> } (named VersionPageProps) rather than with the PageProps globals, as the brief asked.

openQuestions: Should release notes be required to publish, or optional? They are currently required.
Please confirm that system-field limits may be edited (BRD B26 and ARCHITECTURE §2.2) even though the brief said label, help and order only.

Only the seeded master template can be maintained; there is no 'new template' in the UI. A template without a published version, which can only be created outside the UI, would get an empty draft that can never be published, because admins cannot add system sections. Is a single master template enough for Phase 1?
Partners and Viewers get a 404 on /admin/templates, per the brief and the nav. Should they see templates read-only?
Should fields be movable between sections? Currently it is delete and re-add; a field whose key an earlier version used can be re-added under the same key only with the same type.
notesForOtherModules: Routes exposed: /admin/templates (list) and /admin/templates/[versionId] (editor for drafts, read-only otherwise), both for Super Admin and Fund Admin only. The sidebar link already exists in AdminSidebar. No new public routes, database changes or shared-file changes are needed. Integrator: run next typegen/build as usual.

M5 (monthly form): what the builder writes. Picklist and tags options are {"options": string[]} (at least 1, at most 100, no case-insensitive duplicates). Rating options are {"min": int, "max": int} with 0 ≤ min < max ≤ 10 and an optional "labels" object keyed by value, e.g. {"1": "Very low"}; the key is left out when there are no labels. Number-field validation (currency/number/integer/percent) is {"allow_negative": bool, "min"?, "max"?}; the non-negative system figures store no allow_negative (the seed stores {"min": 0}), while gross and net profit may carry allow_negative false. Text/long_text validation is {"max_length": 1–20000}; every other type has null validation.

M5: allowed types per section kind are narrative → long_text/text/picklist/tags/boolean/rating, custom_numbers → currency/number/integer/percent, pulse → rating/long_text/tags/picklist. Admins can rename system fields and sections and add help text to system fields, so always show template labels, not SYSTEM_FIELD_LABELS. Admins can also reorder every section, system ones included, and leave non-system sections empty (only a warning). A section with no fields should render nothing or just its title.

M9 (C4 export): narrative section titles can change between versions and new narrative sections can appear. Section and field keys are stable across versions (create_template_draft copies them; new sections get a slug of their title, unique within the version). If rows must line up across half-years whose months used different versions, match by section key, or by title within each submission's own version.

F-DB / test owners: tests/features/m3/database.test.ts imports tests/db/harness.ts, tests/db/fixtures.ts and tests/db/scenario.ts read-only (freshDb, asUser, expectRule, SEED, save, systemValues, kiddoKpis). If those APIs change, that test needs the same update.

F-LIB (optional): _lib/rules.ts defines SECTION_KIND_NAMES, plain section-kind names for sentences, because SECTION_KIND_LABELS lower-cased reads 'narrative (c4 category)'. It can move to src/lib/constants.ts if other modules want it.
